title: Summer product demo + AMA
summary: Company-wide summer all-hands focused on product demo for the new routing and caching features, readiness for the July pilot, a short ops update on Dedicated capacity, hiring priorities for Q3, and a 20-minute AMA. Leadership recapped metrics and next steps for teams to prepare launch artifacts and security docs.
transcript: 16:00 Nina Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll start in about a minute, but feel free to drop questions in the Q&A. 16:01 Arjun Mehta: Quick mic check, can folks hear me? 16:02 Leah Kim: Yeah, loud and clear. I'm Leah, gonna run the demo and show the new smart-routing UI and the implicit cache stats. 16:03 Samir Patel: Heads up, there's a known display glitch in the demo where KV cache shows as 'KV cash' in some builds, we fixed in staging but you might see the transcription-friendly typo. 16:04 Nina Carter: Love that, Samir. Opening slide — high level plan: ship beta to pilot customers in early July, ramp to GA end of quarter, keep costs predictable. 16:05 Mateo Alvarez: We have three pilot customers confirmed, will share names after legal signs NDAs. 16:07 Leah Kim: Demo start — switching to screen, apologies for a second, there's a bit of lag. so this is the new routing dashboard, you can set policies by latency, cost, or data-residency. 16:08 Speaker 2: (inaudible) — sorry can you zoom in on the policy editor? 16:09 Leah Kim: Sure, zooming, ok in the policy editor you can pick fallback models, set region pins, and assign weights for cost tradeoffs. it's built to be idempotent so rollbacks are quick. 16:10 Arjun Mehta: Under the hood we've changed how the runtime selects kernels. there's now a selection layer that uses sequence-length histograms to pick kernels and quantization profiles. small perf win but compound savings for long-running prompts. 16:12 Nina Carter: Quick product metric check — Leah, what's our expected token throughput improvement? 16:12 Leah Kim: On internal workloads we saw about 18-22% lower p95 latency when routing+cache are enabled, and for embeddings-heavy jobs cost per vector dropped ~12%. results vary by model / seq distribution. 16:14 Anonymous: (chat) will this be available in private deployments? 16:14 Arjun Mehta: Yes, private and on-prem will get the routing layer; customers will be able to opt into the policy engine — we had to adjust a couple KMS flows for HSM-based setups. 16:16 Samir Patel: Ops note — Dedicated pool autoscaling defaults will change; please check your runbooks. There's a new 'burst protect' flag to prevent noisy neighbors. 16:17 Leah Kim: Demo of prefix caching — here's an example where a 3x repeated prefix hits cache and avoids re-compute, you'll see the token breakdown on the right. 16:19 Speaker 3: There's a console metric that jumped yesterday, can we call out what caused the spike? 16:20 Arjun Mehta: That was a load-test that didn't honor the rate limits, our autoscaler handled it but the spike will show in some dashboards for a few hours. we've improved the trace labeling now. 16:21 Nina Carter: Hiring update, Samir? 16:22 Samir Patel: We're opening 18 roles this quarter, focus on infra, runtime, and platform engineers — also a couple of senior product managers. Interviews centralized through TalentOps. target to fill 40% by end of Q3. 16:23 Mateo Alvarez: Sales ops quick note: pricing for Dedicated is getting a small tweak to simplify tiers — we'll publish a FAQ and send to finance. 16:24 Leah Kim: Security/compliance — we shipped the extended audit logs for Private customers last week; ISO gap items are on track. 16:25 Speaker 4: (low) Are we doing any changes to data retention defaults? 16:26 Arjun Mehta: Default retention stays the same for hosted, but Private can configure retention and KMS rotation. we also added a per-route log level setting. 16:27 Nina Carter: Ok let's switch to AMA — ask anything, keep questions short so we can get to many folks. 16:28 Speaker 5: Hey Nina, what's the top risk you see for the July pilot? 16:29 Nina Carter: Good question — capacity misalignment is top risk, we need teams to validate workloads and share realistic traffic patterns. 16:30 Speaker 6: Will there be a public changelog for - the kernels/quantization changes? 16:31 Arjun Mehta: Yes, a changelog + migration notes are going to be posted to the Console docs and pinned in the #release channel. 16:33 Speaker 7: Any update on partnerships with cloud providers? 16:33 Mateo Alvarez: We're in late discussions with two regional partners in APAC, looking to co-locate Dedicated nodes. nothing signed yet. 16:34 Speaker 8: Question about benchmarks — will you publish the raw benchmark spreadsheets? 16:35 Leah Kim: We'll share sanitized benchmarks for public models; partner-specific benchmarks will be shared under NDA. 16:36 Speaker 9: (interruption) can we get more clarity on cost controls for sandbox environments? 16:37 Samir Patel: We'll add quotas and a dev-tier routing policy that forces low-cost models for sandboxes. documentation will include examples. 16:38 Nina Carter: Ok quick recap — pilot readiness, docs, security checklist, and pricing FAQ. who has action items — Leah? 16:40 Leah Kim: Action — publish routing docs and migration notes (owner Leah Kim, due 2025-07-03). 16:41 Samir Patel: Action — ops to update autoscaler defaults and runbooks (owner Samir Patel, due 2025-07-01). 16:42 Mateo Alvarez: Action — sales to finalize pilot terms and distribute NDAs (owner Mateo Alvarez, due 2025-06-30). 16:43 Arjun Mehta: Action — engineering to produce kernel changelog and migration guide (owner Arjun Mehta, due 2025-07-02). 16:44 Speaker 10: Can we get a follow-up deep dive on Private encryption flows? 16:44 Nina Carter: Yes we'll set a technical deep dive next week, Arjun and Samir to lead. 16:45 Speaker 11: Are we adjusting comp or org as part of these hires? 16:46 Nina Carter: Not at this moment; compensation review remains on schedule, org changes will be announced with context. 16:47 Speaker 12: (murmur) will GA have any breaking changes? 16:48 Leah Kim: We're aiming for backward compatibility; any breaking changes will be gated and communicated. 16:49 Speaker 13: Any update on uptime SLA for Dedicated? 16:50 Samir Patel: SLA targets unchanged; we're baking in observability improvements to meet error budgets. 16:51 Nina Carter: Last question, what's one thing each of you is excited about? Arjun? 16:52 Arjun Mehta: Seeing the kernel selection work actually reduce real customer costs — that's my highlight. 16:53 Leah Kim: For me it's the routing UI — it's finally making it trivial for product teams to tune cost/latency tradeoffs. 16:54 Mateo Alvarez: I'm excited about the pilot conversations in APAC — big market there. 16:55 Samir Patel: Hiring great folks and clearing the pipeline so teams can move faster. 16:56 Nina Carter: Great — thanks everyone. We will send slides, changelog links, and the pilot checklist. End of recording.
